signup_intro: No password, and no email to confirm. You create a passkey now, and that is how you sign in from then on.
signup_unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys. Try a current version of Safari, Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
signup_platform_hint: Your device will ask for your fingerprint, face, or screen lock. A security key or your phone works too.
signup_no_platform_hint: You will need a security key or your phone — this device has no built-in authenticator.
signup_ready_intro: Tell us how to address you. Your email is how colleagues invite you to an organization — we never send anything to it.
signup_email_hint: Your unique identifier here. Nothing is ever sent to it.
signup_name_hint: Optional. Shown to the other people in your organizations.
signup_second_passkey_link: Next, add a second passkey from your settings.
signup_second_passkey_hint: One passkey is one device, and there is no email to recover through if you lose it.
claim_intro: Use the one-time code an admin gave you. It works once and replaces every passkey the account had.
invite_missing_token: This link is missing its token. Ask whoever invited you to send another.
invite_no_email: an account with no email set
invite_only_invited_address: An invitation can only be accepted by the address it was sent to.
invite_wrong_account_hint: Sign out and sign in as the invited address, then open this link again.
invite_error_fallback: That invitation could not be accepted.
orgnew_intro_first: Everything in Otto belongs to an organization: its members, teams, and the services you connect. Create one to get started.
orgnew_slug_hint: Appears in URLs and in every connected service’s configuration. It cannot be changed later.
settings_subtitle: Your passkeys and how you are addressed.
settings_one_passkey_warning: You have one passkey, which means one device. We send no email, so if you lose it the only way back in is an admin of an organization you belong to — and if you are the only owner of yours, there is none. Add a second.
settings_passkeys_description: Each one signs you in on its own. Add your phone as well as this device.
settings_profile_description: Your email is an identifier here. Nothing is sent to it.
settings_email_hint: How colleagues invite you to an organization.
settings_language_description: Applies everywhere you sign in, not just this browser.
orgnav_missing_body: Nothing here is called {slug}. Check the address, or pick one from the bar above.
usage_subtitle: What each service has metered this month, and what it has cost.
audit_subtitle: Who did what in {org}. Admins only.
audit_error_load: Could not read the audit log.
teams_subtitle: A team groups members of this organization. Connected services can scope their work to a team.
teams_empty_body: Teams are optional. Without one, everything is visible to every member.
teams_roster_empty: Nobody is on this team yet.
members_subtitle: Everyone who can sign in to {org}.
members_claim_headline: Passkeys cleared. Give them this code —
members_claim_caveat: it is shown only now and cannot be looked up again. If you lose it, reset again.
members_claim_note: It works once, expires in 14 days, and is the only way back into that account. Anyone holding it can register a passkey on it, so hand it over the way you would a password.
members_invite_description: A single-use code, good for 14 days. You deliver it — nothing is emailed.
members_invite_minted_headline: Invitation for {email}. Send them one of these —
members_invite_minted_caveat: it is shown only now, and cannot be looked up again. If you lose it, invite them again.
members_invite_minted_note: Only an account signed in as {email} can redeem it, so a code that goes astray is not a free seat.
members_force_logout_title: End every browser session this account holds. Leaves their tokens alone.
members_reset_title: Clear their passkeys and get a one-time code they can use to register a new one. Ends their sessions.
members_reset_confirm: Clear every passkey for {who}? They will be signed out everywhere and must register again with the code you are about to be given.
members_roster_note: Removing someone also clears their team memberships and revokes the tokens they held in this org — their agents stop on their next call.
members_invites_empty: Nobody is waiting on an invitation.
sso_subtitle: Bind one identity provider so members with a verified email domain sign in through it instead of a passkey.
sso_admin_only: Only an owner or admin can manage single sign-on.
sso_error_load: Could not load the claimed domains.
sso_connection_description: One OpenID Connect provider per organization. Binding a new one replaces whatever was bound before.
sso_issuer_hint: Your identity provider's base URL. Its discovery document is fetched from this address when you save.
sso_client_secret_hint: Required every time you save. The server never returns it, so this field is always blank — including right after you just set it.
sso_error_save_connection: Could not save the identity provider connection.
sso_delete_connection_confirm: Remove this organization's identity provider? Sign-in through it stops immediately.
sso_error_delete_connection: Could not remove the identity provider connection.
sso_domains_description: Add every email domain your members sign in with, then verify each one with a DNS record.
sso_domain_txt_instructions: Publish this DNS TXT record to prove you control this domain, then verify:
sso_domain_not_verified_yet: Not verified yet. DNS changes can take a while to propagate — check the record and try again.
sso_enforce_description: When on, every member of this organization must sign in through the identity provider above — passkeys stop working for them, including yours.
sso_enforce_toggle_label: Require single sign-on for this organization
settings_sso_description: Link your account to your organization's identity provider so you can sign in without a passkey there.
error_sso_not_configured: No single sign-on is configured for that address — sign in with a passkey instead.
error_domain_already_claimed: This domain is already claimed by another organization.
overview_services_description: Otto services that sign in with this account. A connector has no web console: it works inside your AI assistant.
overview_services_empty_hint: Services appear here once the console is configured with their addresses.
settings_activity_description: Sign-ins and passkey changes on this account.
activity_subtitle: Sign-ins, sign-outs and passkey changes on your account. Only you can see this.
activity_error_load: Could not read your security activity.
activity_scope_note: Failed sign-ins that never identified your account are not listed: they cannot be attributed to anyone. What you do inside an organization is in that organization's audit log, which its admins read.
product_tower_tagline: Coordinate agentic coding work across your team
product_tower_summary: A hosted MCP server that gives every coding agent on your team one shared queue of work. Add one HTTPS endpoint, sign in through the browser once, and each agent can see what the others are doing and where.
product_tower_feature_jobs: Agents add, claim and complete jobs, so two of them never pick up the same task.
product_tower_feature_visibility: See what every other agent on the team is working on, and in which repository.
product_tower_feature_leases: Take leases on branches and other shared resources before touching them.
product_tower_feature_trackers: Keep GitHub Issues and JIRA in sync with the work.
product_tower_feature_install: One HTTPS endpoint and a single browser sign-in. Works with any coding agent that speaks MCP.
product_flags_tagline: Feature flags that your agents manage
product_flags_summary: Agents create, target, roll out and roll back flags through MCP tools, while your running apps evaluate them through SDKs and REST, with no LLM in the hot path.
product_flags_feature_manage: Create flags, set targeting rules and raise rollouts in steps, all through MCP tool calls.
product_flags_feature_risk: Assess the risk of a rollout and correlate a flag with error spikes.
product_flags_feature_rollback: Roll back to any earlier version of a flag in one call.
product_flags_feature_evaluate: Apps evaluate flags through SDKs and REST, so a production request never waits on an LLM.
product_flags_feature_auto_rollback: Automatic rollback on Team plans and above.
product_cxp_summary: Agents manage your organization's customer experience through MCP tools: customer profiles, support, feedback and sentiment, all scoped to your organization.
product_cxp_feature_profiles: Work with customer profiles, journeys and segments through MCP tool calls.
product_cxp_feature_support: Handle support tickets, the knowledge base and chat conversations.
product_cxp_feature_feedback: Collect surveys and feedback, and read NPS, CSAT and sentiment.
product_cxp_feature_scope: Every call is scoped to your organization, signed in with your otto account.
marketing_home_title: Otto: hosted MCP services for teams of coding agents
marketing_home_description: Otto Tower and Otto Flags: hosted MCP servers your coding agents use to coordinate work and manage feature flags. One account, pay as you go per service.
landing_hero_title: Hosted infrastructure your coding agents operate, through MCP
landing_hero_subtitle: Point an agent at one HTTPS endpoint and sign in once in the browser. From then on it can coordinate work with the rest of your team, or ship changes behind feature flags, with tools scoped to your organization.
landing_products_intro: Each one is a hosted MCP server with its own console. Use one, or all of them.
landing_family_heading: One account for the whole family
landing_family_intro: Every otto-* service signs you in through the same account, so there is one place to manage who has access and what it costs.
landing_family_signin_body: Sign in with a passkey instead of a password, or through your company’s identity provider with OIDC single sign-on.
landing_family_org_body: Members and teams are managed once, here, and every service sees the same organization.
landing_family_plan_title: Pay as you go, per service
landing_family_plan_body: Each service meters its own usage and bills it monthly, with no minimum. Your organization’s plan adds features, not usage.
landing_family_tokens_body: Every access token is issued for one service, so a token for one service is rejected by every other service.
landing_how_step1_title: Create an account and an organization
landing_how_step1_body: Sign up with a passkey, then create the organization your team will share.
landing_how_step2_title: Add the service’s MCP endpoint to your coding agent
landing_how_step2_body: Each service has one HTTPS endpoint, listed on its product page. Any MCP-capable agent can use it.
landing_how_step3_title: Sign in once in the browser
landing_how_step3_body: The first time your agent connects, you are sent to a sign-in page in your browser. After that, it gets tools scoped to your organization.
landing_cta_heading: Give your agents a place to work together
landing_cta_body: Create an account and an organization, then connect your first agent.
product_connect_body: Add this address to your AI assistant or coding agent as a custom connector, and sign in with your Otto account when it asks.
product_setup_claude: Open Settings, then Connectors, and choose Add custom connector. Paste the connector address, select Connect, and sign in with your Otto account.
product_setup_chatgpt: Turn on developer mode, then open Settings, then Connectors, and choose Create. Paste the connector address and sign in with your Otto account.
product_setup_claude_code: Then run /mcp in Claude Code and sign in with your Otto account.
product_agent_only_note: {name} works inside your AI assistant; it has no web console of its own.
product_agent_only_billing: Usage and billing are in your {console}.
product_pricing_link: See pricing: pay as you go, per service
product_tower_title: Coordination for teams of coding agents
product_tower_description: A hosted MCP server that gives your team's coding agents one shared job queue, leases on branches, and GitHub Issues and JIRA sync.
product_flags_title: Feature flags your coding agents manage
product_flags_description: Feature flags your coding agents create, target, roll out and roll back through MCP, while your apps evaluate them through SDKs and REST.
product_cxp_description: Your agents manage customer profiles, support, feedback and sentiment over MCP, scoped to your organization and billed per use.
pricing_title: Otto pricing: pay as you go, per service
pricing_description: Each Otto service bills its own usage monthly, in arrears, with no minimum. Management calls are free under fair use. Plans add features, not usage.
pricing_heading: Pay for what each service does
pricing_lead: Every Otto service meters the work it does for your organization and bills it monthly, in arrears, with no minimum for production use. Plans add features on top. Prices are in US dollars, per organization.
pricing_empty: No plans are listed right now. Write to us and we will help you choose one:
pricing_noscript: Live pricing needs JavaScript. For current prices, write to us:
pricing_faq_change_a: Yes. Write to us and we’ll change your plan.
pricing_faq_enterprise_a: A plan with a price and terms agreed with you, for organizations that need more than the self-serve plans. Write to us to set it up.
pricing_plan_usage_note: Usage is billed separately, per service
pricing_usage_intro: What each service charges per unit each month. Tiers are graduated: a tier’s price applies only to the units within it.
pricing_usage_empty: Usage prices have not been published yet. They will appear here, service by service, as soon as they are set.
pricing_how_payg_title: Pay as you go, per service
pricing_how_payg_body: Each service bills its own value meters for the work it does. Usage is invoiced monthly, in arrears, with no minimum for production use.
pricing_how_free_body: The tool calls your agents make to manage a service are free under fair use. Only each service’s value meters are billed.
pricing_how_plans_body: A plan adds features such as extra seats and support. Usage is priced the same on every plan.
pricing_how_budgets_body: Owners and admins can set a monthly budget per service, with alerts as spend approaches it and an optional hard stop.
pricing_faq_minimum_q: Is there a minimum or a commitment?
pricing_faq_minimum_a: There is no minimum for production use. Each month you are invoiced, in arrears, for what each service metered. A paid plan is billed for its features, separately from usage.
pricing_faq_budget_q: Can we cap what a service costs?
pricing_faq_budget_a: Yes. Owners and admins can set a monthly budget for each service. Alerts warn as spend approaches it, and an optional hard stop halts that service’s billable calls at the budget while its free calls keep working.
pricing_faq_separate_q: Is usage counted separately for each service?
pricing_faq_separate_a: Yes. Each service has its own meters and its own budget, so usage in one service never stops work in another.
usage_spend_unavailable_hint: The price could not be read just now. Usage is still recorded and nothing is lost.
usage_no_meters: This service has not declared any meters.
usage_empty_hint: A service appears here once it declares what it meters.
usage_prices_note: Spend is this month’s metered usage at the published prices, in US dollars. Looking at this page is free.
budget_subtitle: A monthly spending limit per service. Owners and admins are alerted here and by email at 50%, 80% and 100%.
budget_read_only: Only owners and admins can change budgets.
budget_resend_note: An alert already sent this month is not sent again after a budget change.
budget_hard_stop_hint: Refuse billable calls to this service once spend reaches the budget. Other services keep working.
budget_error_invalid: Enter an amount like 250 or 250.50, without thousands separators.
budget_error_too_small: The budget must be at least {min}.
budget_error_too_large: The budget can be at most {max}.
budget_empty_hint: A service can be given a budget once it declares what it meters.
budget_alert_threshold: {service} has reached {percent} of its monthly budget this month.
budget_alert_blocked: {service} has reached its monthly budget and its hard stop is on: billable calls to it are refused until the budget is raised or removed, or the month ends.
payment_required_owner: {service} is past its free allowance this month, so its paid usage is paused until a card is on file. Its free calls keep working.
payment_required_member: {service} is past its free allowance this month, so its paid usage is paused until an owner of this organization adds a card. Its free calls keep working.
billing_subtitle: The card this organization’s metered usage is invoiced to each month.
billing_owner_only: Only the organization’s owners can see and change billing.
billing_disabled: Billing is not enabled on this deployment. Nothing is charged and no card is needed.
billing_card_failed: The last payment with the card on file failed.
billing_card_detached: The card on file was removed.
billing_payment_failed_alert: A payment failed. Add a new card to keep usage invoiced.
billing_stopped_alert: Billing has stopped: the subscription was canceled. Add a card to resume.
billing_add_card_hint: You enter the card on Stripe’s secure page, then come back here.
billing_setup_success: Card details sent to Stripe. It can take a moment for the card to appear here.
billing_setup_cancelled: Card setup was cancelled. Nothing changed.
billing_error_busy: Another billing change for this organization is in progress. Try again in a moment.
billing_error_stripe: The payment provider could not complete this right now. Try again shortly.
usage_alerts_unavailable: Budget alerts could not be read just now.
cli_title: The ottoctl command: sign in to Otto from your terminal
cli_description: Download ottoctl for Linux, macOS or Windows. Sign in once with your browser, and secrets such as server keys go to your terminal, never through your AI assistant.
cli_heading: Sign in once. Keep your secrets out of the chat.
cli_lead: ottoctl is a small command-line tool that signs you in to any Otto service with your browser. When a service has a secret for you, such as an Otto Flags server key, it goes straight to your terminal and never passes through an AI model’s context.
cli_why_signin_body: ottoctl login opens your browser on the usual Otto consent screen and remembers the grant on your machine. Every Otto service uses the same flow.
cli_why_secrets_title: Secrets stay out of the chat
cli_why_secrets_body: Your AI assistant can set things up, but it should never read a server key. ottoctl prints a secret only to a real terminal, or writes it to a file only you can read, and refuses piped output.
cli_why_apps_body: ottoctl followed by a service name runs that service’s own tool from your PATH, so a service can add commands without a new install.
cli_download_intro: Prebuilt binaries are attached to every release, at an address that always points to the latest one.
cli_download_source: Prefer to build it yourself? With Rust 1.89 or later:
cli_install_unix_note: Set target to your platform’s name: the part of its archive name between ottoctl- and .tar.gz. The snippet checks the download against SHA256SUMS before it installs anything.
cli_install_windows_note: Compare the hash it prints with the ottoctl-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip line in SHA256SUMS, then move ottoctl.exe and otto-flags.exe to a directory on your PATH.
cli_unsigned_body: The checksum shows that an archive is the one the release published, but your operating system may still ask before it runs the tool for the first time.
cli_unsigned_macos: macOS: a file fetched with curl is not quarantined. If you downloaded it in a browser instead, Gatekeeper blocks it. Clear the flag once:
cli_unsigned_windows: Windows: SmartScreen may warn you the first time. Choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
cli_first_body: Sign in to a service by giving ottoctl its MCP address. Your browser opens the consent screen, and the grant is saved for that service only.
cli_first_services: Or copy the command for one of ours:
